question: Which grows fastest in a typical recent year: credit card debt, a mortgage, money in shares, or money in savings?
answer: Card debt, at about 21.5% a year in the US in 2024, more than double the stock market's long-run average of about 10%. Paying off a card balance is a sure 21.5% return, which no investment promises; investing while the balance rolls over means borrowing at 21.5% to earn perhaps 10.
move: Paying off expensive debt is an investment with a guaranteed return.
source: Federal Reserve G.19; Freddie Mac; FDIC; Siegel
reference: Federal Reserve Statistical Release G.19, Consumer Credit (2024); Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (2024); FDIC National Rates and Rate Caps (2024); Siegel, Stocks for the Long Run, 6th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2022
ask: Do I carry a card balance while putting money into investments?

items.label: Mortgage
items.note: About 6.7% in 2024, for a 30-year fixed loan.

items.label: Shares
items.note: About 10% a year on average since 1926, with bad years on the way.

items.label: Savings account
items.note: The 2024 national average; even the best accounts paid a fraction of card rates.

items.label: Credit card
items.note: About 21.5%: clearing it beats the stock market's average twice over.
